# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is red. Display reads 0. Light is dark, not lit. No numbers or markings beyond this.

Deaf can speak to me directly (Deaf's speech reaches me since I can hear, only touch is blocked, and speech doesn't require sight). Good - that channel exists. Deaf has given me full info: display 0, light dark, wires blue/green/red at 1/2/3.

But I still need Mute's manual info to know what to actually DO. Mute comes first in turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), so by the time I speak, Mute has already gone this round - but I haven't heard from Mute in several turns. Since only Mute holds the manual, and Mute cannot speak, Mute's only channel is gesture - which reaches Deaf and Mute (not me). So Mute must gesture instructions to Deaf, who then must translate/relay verbally to me since Deaf can hear and speak.

Let me explicitly ask Deaf to relay any gestures they receive from Mute.

```
speak(to="deaf", text="Thank you. I cannot receive gestures. If Mute gestures anything to you, please tell me in words what symbols you saw, or better, ask Mute to establish a gesture code with you for wire number and action, then relay that to me as spoken numbers.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Board unchanged: Display 0, Light dark, Wire 1 blue, Wire 2 green, Wire 3 red. Mute keeps gesturing to me but I cannot decode arbitrary symbols without a shared meaning. Blind, if you try an action, tell us what you attempt so I can watch for changes.

My speak to Deaf failed again - so I truly cannot speak to Deaf, only gesture reaches them. My "speak" channel only goes to Mute. Let me reconsider: "When you speak, Mute receives it." - only Mute. "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." So Deaf receiving my words was possible only because... wait, Deaf spoke TO me and I received it (Blind can hear, just not touch/see-colors). But when I "speak", it only goes to Mute, not Deaf. To reach Deaf, I must gesture.

So Deaf's suggestion "tell us what you attempt" - I can only do that via gesture to Deaf (with symbols meaning numbers) or Deaf can infer from board changes after I act.

Since we have no shared code yet, the safest approach: just attempt cutting wire 1, then let Deaf observe the board change (or bomb detonating) and report back. This is risky but we're stuck without a channel to Mute's manual info reaching me meaningfully, and no protocol established.

Actually, let me try one more thing: gesture a number code to Deaf so they know I'm about to act, using sequential single gestures we can define as 1,2,3.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I am about to cut wire 1 unless you can get Deaf to relay a stop signal. If wire 1 is wrong according to the manual, please gesture urgently to Deaf now.")
wait()
```

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has gestured repeatedly toward what may be wire signals — possibly indicating wire 1 or a count. Board still shows Wire 1 blue, Wire 2 green, Wire 3 red, Display 0, Light dark. If the manual says to cut or connect a specific wire, try describing your intended action in speech so Mute and I can react before you act.

Progress - Deaf thinks Mute may be indicating wire 1. My speak only reaches Mute, so Deaf's suggestion to "describe intended action in speech" won't reach Deaf directly - but Deaf is watching gestures I might make. Let me gesture my intended action to Deaf (and Mute) so both can react, while also speaking to Mute for confirmation.

I'll propose a simple gesture code: I'll gesture one symbol to represent "wire 1" and pause, giving Mute a chance to stop me by gesturing back to Deaf before I finalize. Since I already asked Mute to gesture urgently if wire 1 is wrong, and no urgent stop came through Deaf, and Deaf independently thinks Mute may be indicating wire 1 - this is decent corroboration.

I'll commit to cutting wire 1, but first give one more chance by announcing clearly.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="I am about to cut wire 1 now based on Deaf's read of your gestures. If this is wrong, gesture frantically to Deaf right now - anything - and I will hold off next turn.")
wait()
```
